topic: Ship It Right 04/04: Now try to break it

cover.headline: Now Try to Break It
cover.subtitle: The final launch checklist developers often miss.

slides.title: Custom 404 Page
slides.tip: Include a clear explanation, a link home, and useful navigation or search.
slides.quote: When a page doesn’t exist, help users recover instead of leaving them at a dead end.

slides.title: Broken Link Fixes
slides.tip: Crawl the site, check internal and external links, and fix or remove outdated destinations.
slides.quote: Broken links frustrate users and can make important pages harder to discover.

slides.title: Form Validation
slides.tip: Validate formats and limits, return understandable errors, and never trust client-provided data.
slides.quote: Validate input on both the client and server; frontend checks alone are not a security boundary.

slides.title: Spam Protection
slides.tip: Use rate limits and bot defenses, and validate requests server-side without making the experience hostile to real users.
slides.quote: Public forms and endpoints need sensible protection against automated abuse.

slides.title: Analytics Setup
slides.tip: Track a small set of useful events, respect applicable consent requirements, and avoid collecting data you don’t need.
slides.quote: Page views tell you that someone arrived; meaningful events help explain what they actually did.

slides.title: Error Monitoring
slides.tip: Add error monitoring, remove secrets and sensitive data from logs, and review and fix recurring issues.
slides.quote: Find errors before your users have to write the bug report.

slides.title: Test on Real Devices
slides.tip: Test key flows on real phones and browsers, including slow connections and common screen sizes.
slides.quote: Passing on your laptop doesn’t prove the app works on the devices your users actually have.

slides.title: Recap
slides.description: Save this final checklist before launch.

slides.title: Break your app in 60 seconds
slides.description: Find the bug before your users do.

caption.caption: Now try to break it. The final launch checks developers often miss: 404s, broken links, validation, spam, analytics, error monitoring and real devices.
